label: B25-M20K-READ-ALIGNMENT

root_cause_proof.model: A test-only altera_syncram stub samples address/data at clock0 and updates q_a/q_b after the edge. A separate posedge process therefore observes the previous q value, matching the synchronous M20K timing property hidden by the behavioral byte array.

failures: first PC=0-equivalent read actual=0x8877665544332216 (parked word 7), expected=0x8877665544332211 (word 0)
next aligned word read actual=0x8877665544332211 (word 0), expected=0x8877665544332210 (word 1)
pre_fix_rtl.interpretation: The old request and debug wrappers returned the previous synchronous RAM word. Reset-time address-zero precharge could hide only the first fetch; the next changed address remained stale.

changes: Make port-A address/data/byte-enable/read-control registers explicit at CLOCK0, matching the intended synchronous M20K contract.
On req_accept, capture word address, byte offset and read/write response kind; drive the live accepted address on that edge and hold it until rsp_ready retires the response.
Return read data directly from the post-edge q_a shifted by the captured offset instead of capturing the previous q_a in the accept-edge always_ff.
Capture debug byte offset on the same edge as the synchronous port-B address and combine it with post-edge q_b, eliminating the extra stale-data register.

commit_timing.request: held address/offset/kind and fault update only on req_accept
commit_timing.write: existing byte-enabled write side effect remains on req_accept edge
commit_timing.read: rsp_valid becomes visible after the accept edge with the corresponding post-edge q_a and remains stable under backpressure
commit_timing.debug: dbg_addr and dbg_off are associated on one edge; post-edge q_b and captured offset form dbg_rdata

unchanged: behavioral RAM implementation and byte-address semantics
public single-outstanding and one-cycle response contract
QSF, SDC, generated vendor IP, boot image and software
